//: Routing order on Vercel is: redirects -> filesystem -> rewrites. Every route is
prerendered to its own folder by prerender.js, so the filesystem answers real URLs
and the rewrites below only fire for paths with no file behind them.
The previous catch-all rewrite ('/(.*)' -> '/index.html') meant EVERY unknown URL
returned HTTP 200 with the SPA shell. Google treats that as a soft 404: crawl budget
is spent on URLs that do not exist, and they inflate the not-indexed count. Dropping
it lets unmatched paths fall through to 404.html with a real 404 status.
/blog/:slug keeps an explicit rewrite because posts live in the CMS: a post published
after the last build has no prerendered file yet, and must still open in the SPA
rather than 404. Crawlers never reach this path - middleware.js renders those
server-side before the filesystem is consulted.
